subject: general
question: In the case of reflection of light from a concave mirror, when a parallel beam of light is incident on the reflecting surface, reflected light ________.

options.text: appears to converge at the centre of curvature
appears to diverge from the principal focus
appears to diverge from the centre of curvature
appears to converge at the principal focus

solution:
The correct answer is __**appears to converge at the principal focus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a parallel beam of light is incident on a concave mirror, it reflects and converges at a single point called the principal focus.
 
• The principal focus of a concave mirror is the point where parallel rays of light meet after reflection.
 
• The distance between the mirror's surface and the principal focus is known as the focal length.
 
• The center of curvature is the center of the sphere from which the concave mirror segment is taken.
 
• The principal axis is the line that passes through the center of curvature and the midpoint of the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirror**

 
 
• A convex mirror diverges parallel beams of light, making them appear to originate from a point behind the mirror called the virtual focus.
 
• Convex mirrors are used in vehicles as rear-view mirrors due to their wider field of view.
 
 
 
• **Reflection Laws**
 
 
• The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
 
• The incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal to the surface all lie in the same plane.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Concave Mirrors**
 
 
• Concave mirrors are used in telescopes to gather and focus light.
 
• They are also used in headlights of vehicles to focus light beams into parallel rays.
